title: Banking Basics
blurb: Accounts, cards and fees in plain language.
cards: A current or checking account holds money for daily use. A savings account is for money you do not touch and often pays interest. Keep them separate.
Which account is best for money you want to grow and not spend?
Savings accounts earn interest and discourage spending.
Some accounts charge monthly fees, ATM fees or overdraft charges. Read the fee list and pick an account that fits how you use money.
Overdrafts are a free safety net.
They are borrowing, often with fees or high interest.
Debit vs credit card: what is the main difference?
Debit spends your own money, credit borrows from the lender
A debit card draws on your balance. A credit card borrows money you must repay.
You lose your card. What do you do first?
Freeze or cancel it right away through your bank
Freeze it immediately to stop misuse, then ask for a replacement.
example: An account charges $3 each month and another charges $24 a year. Their base fee can be the same over a full year, but check transaction and ATM fees too.
